title: Data Analytics & Automation Specialist
desc: Hours: Full-Time – 35 Hours Work Location: 30-30 Thomson Avenue, LIC, NY 11101 The Technology and Innovation Division (T&I) within the New York City Department of Design and Construction (DDC) seeks to hire a skilled, data-driven Data Analytics & Automation Specialist. DDC is the City’s primary capital construction agency, responsible for delivering safe, sustainable, and innovative public buildings and infrastructure across the five boroughs. Partnering with client agencies, design professionals, and the construction industry, DDC manages a broad portfolio of projects from firehouses, libraries, and community centers to roadways, sewers, and resiliency initiatives helping to shape a more equitable, efficient, and resilient city. Through its commitment to design excellence, technological modernization, and public service, DDC ensures that critical civic projects are delivered on time, on budget, and to the highest standards of quality. The Technology and Innovation (T&I) Division serves as DDC’s centralized Information, Technology, and Telecom operation, organized into four core units: Network, Infrastructure and Security; Service Delivery; Application Development, and Administrative Analytics. Together, these units provide the hardware, software, enterprise applications, and data ecosystem that support the agency’s daily operations. In addition to maintaining core systems, the division leads strategic modernization efforts aimed at improving efficiency, strengthening security, and advancing programmatic excellence across the agency. Reporting directly to the Director of Administrative Analytics, the Data Analytics & Automation Specialist will blend business intelligence and reporting with hands-on data engineering and automation. The selected candidate will build the dashboards leadership relies on and the automated pipelines that feed them across HR, budget, contracting, procurement, and other administrative functions. The ideal candidate will combine strong technical skills in business intelligence, SQL, Python, and automation with excellent communication and interpersonal skills, and will be comfortable working directly with non-technical users to gather requirements, conceptualize business challenges, and deliver practical solutions. This role involves working with sensitive and sometimes confidential data, including personnel information and internal agency operations. The selected candidate will emphasize security and access control in the design of pipelines, the distribution of reports and tools, and the infrastructure that hosts this data. The responsibilities include: - Design, develop, and maintain interactive dashboards, reports, and data visualizations using Power BI, Tableau, or similar tools, including recurring and ad hoc reporting for agency leadership. - Write and maintain SQL queries to extract, transform, validate, and analyze data from agency databases and citywide systems. - Develop Python scripts, ETL processes, and automated pipelines to integrate data from multiple sources, replace manual data handling, and improve the speed, reliability, and accuracy of reporting. - Design and build Power Automate workflows and Power Apps to automate multi-step administrative processes, such as approvals, tracking, and data intake, and integrate them with other agency systems. - Build and maintain data models and automated reporting processes to improve the reliability, efficiency, and integrity of administrative reporting. - Identify opportunities to leverage automation, advanced analytics, and emerging technologies to modernize administrative processes across the agency. Additionally, educational credentials must be from a U.S. Department of Education-recognized accredited institution. Credentials from foreign institutions require independent equivalency verification from an approved evaluation service. A list of providers (fees apply) is available at: https://www.nyc.gov/assets/dcas/downloads/pdf/employment/nyc-dcas-foreign-education-evaluation-guide.pdf. All applicants, including City Employees: Please go to NYC Government Jobs | Explore Careers | City of New York, go to Search for Open Jobs, and type in the Job ID # listed above. Submit job application as prompted. Do not apply via Employee Self-Service (ESS), e-mail, mail, or fax your resume to DDC directly. IT PROJECT SPECIALIST - 95710 1. A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college in computer science, engineering, human computer interaction, interactive media, digital and graphics design, data visualization, communication or a related field, and four years of satisfactory full-time experience related to the area(s) required by the particular position and a specialization in a relevant technology, process, methodology and/or domain; or 2. An associate degree from an accredited college in computer science, engineering, human computer interaction, interactive media, digital and graphics design, data visualization, communication or a related field, and six years of satisfactory full-time experience related to the area(s) required by the particular position and a specialization in a relevant technology, process, methodology and/or domain; or 3. A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college, and eight years of satisfactory full-time experience related to the area(s) required by the particular position and a specialization in a relevant technology, process, methodology and/or domain; or 4. Education and/or experience which is equivalent to "1", "2", or "3" above. The City of New York is an inclusive

title: Data Engineer
desc: The New York City Department of Sanitation (DSNY) keeps New York City healthy, safe, and clean by collecting, recycling, and disposing of waste, cleaning City streets and vacant lots, and clearing snow and ice. DSNY is the nation's largest municipal sanitation agency, with nearly 10,000 employees, 59 district garages, and a fleet of more than 5,000 trucks, cars, and other types of equipment. The Department clears litter, snow, and ice from approximately 6,500 miles of City streets and removes debris from vacant lots as well as abandoned vehicles from City streets. Under general supervision, with considerable latitude for the exercise of independent judgment and initiative, the incumbent will be responsible for the design, development, implementation, enhancement, documentation, and maintenance of database management systems, data integration solutions, custom applications, and related software functions supporting the Department of Sanitation's Operations Management Division (OMD). The selected candidate will serve as a Data Engineer, performing complex data engineering, data integration, and analytical functions within a multi-platform enterprise environment. The role will support critical reporting, analytics, and operational initiatives across the DSNY Operations Management project portfolio. Key Responsibilities: - Perform data analysis, data profiling, data modeling, source-to-target mapping, and reporting activities for enterprise data and analytics projects. - Develop and maintain conceptual, logical, and physical data models to support current and future operational, analytical, and reporting requirements. - Analyze legacy and strategic source systems to assess data quality, identify inconsistencies, and recommend corrective actions to improve data integrity and governance. - Collaborate with business stakeholders, technical teams, and external partners to design, develop, and support complex data integration pipelines using ETL tools such as Databricks, Informatica PowerCenter, Pentaho Data Integration (Kettle), and similar technologies. - Develop, maintain, and enhance technical documentation, including data models, data dictionaries, source-to-target mapping documents, ETL specifications, process flows, and reporting artifacts. - Develop and maintain SQL-based data solutions, including complex queries, stored procedures, database objects, and data transformation processes. - Support business intelligence and reporting initiatives through the development of reports, dashboards, and analytical solutions utilizing platforms such as Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition (OBIEE), Power BI, and other enterprise reporting tools. - Participate in the design and implementation of innovative data architecture and integration strategies to improve data sharing and interoperability across multiple business domains within DSNY and across City agencies. - Support and maintain internal IT systems, applications, and databases, ensuring reliability, performance, and adherence to agency standards. Required Qualifications: - Strong proficiency in SQL and Python programming. title: Analytics & Reporting Engineer for the Division of Strategic Operations & Analytics
desc: About the Agency: The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City. As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike. Your Team: The Office of Policy and Strategy (OPS) leverage its expertise to guide and support HPD and its many Offices in their efforts to deepen their impact, optimize their efficiency, and become more data-driven, climate-adaptive, and mission-focused. As part of OPS, the Division of Strategic Operations and Analytics (SOA) works to increase HPD's impact by analyzing and improving operations agency-wide. SOA does this by clarifying HPD program missions, objectives, and stakeholders; implementing initiatives that advance HPD's goals; analyzing data to deliver actionable insights to HPD programs; and increasing the agency's overall ability to leverage data. Your Impact: As the Analytics & Reporting Engineer within SOA, you will play a key role in making HPD’s data more accessible, reliable, and reusable to support reporting and analytics. By building well-structured datasets, automations and data flows, you will help SOA and other HPD offices turn data into key reporting and metrics that support key agency programs for New Yorkers. Your Role: Your role will focus on hands-on development of data pipelines, curating datasets and data flows in SQL Server and building reusable scripts and code to support reporting and analytics work for agency programs such as homeless placement services, homebuyer assistance, housing distress & compliance, and fair housing work. You will also create and maintain reports and dashboards, or related dataflows/models. Exercising independent judgement and initiative, you will implement solutions through scalable data models, automated workflows, and well-structured datasets and BI data flows - to enable more efficient reporting, research, and analytics for key agency programs. Your Responsibilities: - Build and maintain core datasets, data models, and dashboards to support key program reporting and analytics - Build and automate Python-based data cleaning and integration pipelines merging data across siloed source systems and using automation tools to support reporting needs for housing placements, fair housing and more. - Load cleaned datasets into SQL Server and connect to BI tools (e.g. Power BI) to support reporting/dashboarding. - Implement basic code validation, testing, and documentation practices to keep analytics scripts and datasets reliable and maintainable. - Document code standards and workflows so datasets and scripts remain usable/maintainable by the team over time. - Apply data engineering skills and creative collaboration techniques to address technical issues and drive the approach for the team Preferred skills - Inquisitive, self-motivated problem-solver who is passionate about making organizations more data-driven - Comfortable working in a fast-moving, resource-constrained environment with messy data and legacy systems; motivated by rolling up your sleeves and building practical tools that make a real impact on people's lives. - Experience building or supporting data pipelines (ETL/ELT) extracting, cleaning, and transforming data from multiple sources. - Experience working with relational databases (e.g., SQL Server or similar) - Some experience with BI data modeling (preferably Power BI or similar) is a plus - Familiarity with source control and version control workflows (e.g., Azure DevOps Repos) - Strong interpersonal and organizational skills; able to ask thoughtful questions and collaborate across teams - Strong aptitude for learning new tools and technologies independently using online resources - Technical skills: SQL, Python, Power BI data modeling (DAX, Power Query M), and data modeling fundamentals CITY RESEARCH SCIENTIST - 21744 1.
